newsitem.title: USA: Labor Secy Reich sees no slowing of U.S. economy.
newsitem.headline: Labor Secy Reich sees no slowing of U.S. economy.

text.p: Labor Secretary Robert Reich said Tuesday that he expected the U.S. economy to continue growing without triggering higher inflation.
"Predictions are always hazardous, but I see no sign of a slowdown at all," Reich told reporters after addressing the Center for National Policy, a research group.

"We seem to have a continuation of this marvelous 'Goldilocks economy'," he said, referring to a label he had previously put on the economy to indicate that it was not too hot, not too cold, but just right.
Reich reiterated that he sees no evidence of upward wage pressures triggering higher inflation.
"They said it couldn't be done, but we are combining very strong economic growth without any apparent sign of spiralling inflation," he said.
Last week, the Commerce Department estimated that the economy grew at a 4.8 percent annual rate in the second quarter.

Responding to a reporter's question, Reich said he saw no reason for concern over a potential impact on the U.S. economy from the latest hostilities in Iraq, but added, "But that is really a little bit beyond my territory."
